intro: Bitcoin punched through to a three-month high near $80,000 on record ETF inflows, while OpenAI and Anthropic both pushed their coding-agent tech into new territory — OpenAI toward non-engineers, Anthropic toward Slack channels that talk back unprompted.

items.headline: OpenAI pushes ChatGPT Work, its Codex-based agent, out to non-engineers
items.summary: OpenAI is extending its Codex-derived agent tooling beyond software engineers through ChatGPT Work, a $20/month tier that lets non-technical staff delegate multistep tasks the way developers already use Codex. The company says internal Codex adoption is near-universal, but outside users of the joint Work/Codex app remain a fraction of ChatGPT's broader user base.
items.why: Shows OpenAI treating its coding-agent stack as the base layer for a much broader agent platform, not just a dev tool.

items.headline: Codex CLI adds an agents dashboard, then deprecates its built-in MCP server
items.summary: OpenAI's Codex CLI 0.149.0 shipped an interactive dashboard for managing concurrent agent tasks plus expanded Vim-style editing; the 0.149.1 patch four days later deprecated the codex mcp-server command, pointing users instead to the Codex app server or the official Codex plugin for Claude Code.
items.why: Notable that OpenAI is now steering its own CLI users toward interoperating directly inside a competitor's tool.

items.headline: Anthropic upgrades Claude's Slack agent to read whole conversations before jumping in
items.summary: Claude Tag, Anthropic's Slack-based agent, now reads a channel's full conversation history plus its memory and standing instructions before choosing to reply inline, start a thread, route the message elsewhere, or say nothing. Anthropic says the change makes it roughly 30% better at knowing when not to intervene.
items.why: Part of Anthropic's push toward agents that act inside team workflows proactively, without being tagged each time.

items.headline: Nvidia in talks to invest in Perplexity at a $30 billion-plus valuation
items.summary: Nvidia is discussing a new funding round for Perplexity that could value the AI search startup above $30 billion, more than 50% higher than a year ago, as Perplexity's annualized revenue climbs past $750 million.
items.why: Another sign of Nvidia recycling AI-hardware profits into equity stakes across the model and application layer.

items.headline: Personal AI assistant 'Instinct' draws privacy backlash over sweeping terms of service
items.summary: Early testers of the private-beta assistant Instinct are circulating its terms of service, which grant the company a broad, perpetual license to users' screen captures, keystrokes, and other device data, and let the AI enter binding agreements on a user's behalf.
items.why: A preview of the consent and data-access fights that come with agents empowered to act on a user's behalf.

items.headline: DeepMind-alumni startup Inherent says its research agent beat Anthropic and OpenAI at replicating studies
items.summary: Inherent, founded by former Google DeepMind researchers, says its AI research agent outperformed larger models from Anthropic and OpenAI at reproducing the findings of published scientific papers — a benchmark for how independently AI can verify and extend research.
items.why: A smaller lab beating frontier incumbents on a research-replication benchmark, rather than a generic leaderboard, is a meaningful capability signal.

items.headline: Next.js warns of an upcoming critical security release
items.summary: Vercel published advance notice that Next.js will ship a scheduled security release on Aug. 26 patching versions 16.3 and 15.5, including a fix for one critical-severity denial-of-service vulnerability in Server Components.
items.why: Teams running Next.js on Server Components should plan the upgrade before the patch lands.

items.headline: SvelteKit 3's release-candidate milestone closes out, clearing the way for stable
items.summary: The SvelteKit 3.0 GitHub milestone hit 100% completion on Aug. 24 with all 157 tracked issues closed, following the release candidate that ships non-experimental typed environment variables and requires Vite 8.
items.why: Signals a stable SvelteKit 3 launch is close, ending a multi-month RC cycle.

items.headline: DeepSeek scraps weekend peak pricing for its API
items.summary: DeepSeek stopped charging its higher weekday peak rate on weekends starting Aug. 23, so Saturday and Sunday API usage is now billed at the lower off-peak rate regardless of time of day.
items.why: A small but telling data point in the price competition among model providers that developers build against.

items.headline: Bitcoin hits a three-month high near $80,000 as momentum returns
items.summary: Bitcoin rose as high as $81,257 on Aug. 25, its best level since mid-May, extending a rally that saw it gain roughly 22-23% over the prior week — the biggest weekly jump in about three years — on the back of falling Treasury yields, renewed White House support for crypto, and billions in forced short-position liquidations.
items.why: The clearest, most consequential bitcoin move of the day, with real capital flows behind it.

items.headline: US spot bitcoin ETFs post their strongest inflow week since October
items.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs pulled in about $1.92 billion in net inflows over the week through Aug. 21, their largest weekly haul since October's cycle peak, as institutional buying reinforced the price rally.
items.why: Institutional ETF demand, not just short covering, is a key test of whether the rally has staying power.

items.headline: Bitcoin mining difficulty holds near its 2026 low as miners face a crossroads
items.summary: Mining difficulty sits just 0.7% above the year's low after ten downward adjustments against only seven increases in 2026, with roughly 150 EH/s of sidelined hashpower that could return quickly if bitcoin's price gains hold, which would erode the difficulty discount current miners are enjoying.
items.why: Whether price strength pulls sidelined miners back online will shape mining economics for the rest of the year.
